Development of an Educational Platform for Reinforcement Learning Control of a Rotary Inverted Pendulum Based on LW-RCP
papers.summary: This study proposes a compact rotary inverted pendulum experimental platform designed for implementing reinforcement learning (RL) based controllers on physical systems. While RL demonstrates superior performance in simulated environments, applying it to real-world systems often leads to performance degradation and instability due to the sim-to-real gap and physical actuator constraints. papers.title: Sample-Efficient Low-Level Motion Planning for Robotic Manipulation Tasks via Zero-Shot Transfer Learning
Design, control and computational strategies for unstructured robotic applications
papers.summary: Modern robotics has moved from tightly scripted, structured workcells to unstructured, open-world settings. This shift replaces fixed fixtures and repeatable parts with deformable objects, occlusions, and changing contacts. As a result, manipulation now hinges on perception-driven control, uncertainty handling, and learning from data. We embrace this transition and show how combining model-based priors with adaptive policies enables reliable performance beyond the lab. papers.title: Robot assistants during high mental workload: Understanding Task-Specific Load in Human–Robot Interaction
papers.summary: Cognitive offloading refers to the redistribution of task demands with the aim of reducing an individual’s mental workload. A promising strategy in this domain involves leveraging robotic agents, whether humanoid or non-humanoid, to support such task redistribution. However, this process is not straightforward, as the effectiveness of a robot as an offloading agent critically depends on identifying the specific type of mental workload experienced by the user. papers.summary: The agroecological transition aims to reduce pesticide use while maintaining the productivity and resilience of farming systems. papers.title: Scaling vision models does not consistently improve localisation-based explanation quality
papers.summary: Artificial intelligence models are increasingly scaled to improve predictive accuracy, yet it remains unclear whether scale improves the quality of post-hoc explanations. We investigate this relationship by evaluating 11 computer vision models representing increasing levels of depth and complexity within the ResNet, DenseNet, and Vision Transformer families, trained from scratch or pretrained, across the medical and natural image datasets with ground-truth segmentation masks. papers.title: State-based Selection of Expert Policies in Disaster Environments and Reinforcement Learning of a Unified Student Policy via Distillation
EEG: Probabilistic Selection and Depression
papers.summary: This dataset contains EEG recordings from 122 college-age participants performing a probabilistic selection task, collected circa 2008-2010 in the John J.B. Allen laboratory at the University of Arizona. Participants were selected based on reliably high or low scores on the Beck Depression Inventory, with some undergoing clinical interviews. The dataset supports investigation of reinforcement learning and reward-based decision-making processes in relation to depression.

papers.summary: This dataset contains original soybean seed images developed for computer vision and object detection research, with a focus on the detection of healthy and damaged soybean seeds. The dataset contains two classes: healthy seeds and damaged seeds. The original images are provided in their original form, together with corresponding annotations for object detection.
